Here's How Much You'd Have If You Invested $1000 in Monolithic Power a Decade Ago
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:30 AM CDT 3 min read
For most investors, how much a stock's price changes over time is important. This factor can impact your investment portfolio as well as help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.
The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.
What if you'd invested in Monolithic Power (MPWR) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to MPWR for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?
With that in mind, let's take a look at Monolithic Power's main business drivers.
Monolithic Power Systems, based in Kirkland, WA, designs, develops and markets high-performance power solutions. The company focuses on the market for high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs).
Monolithic's products are widely used in industrial applications, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud computing, and automotive and consumer applications.
Being a fabless company, Monolithic works with third-party contractors and chip assemblers for the manufacturing, assembling and testing of wafers and ICs. This approach permits the company to focus more on the designing and development of process technology at a lower fixed cost.
Unlike other fabless semiconductor companies, Monolithic installs its own proprietary process technologies in third-party contractors' equipment and facilities.
Monolithic reported total revenues of $980.6 million in the second quarter of 2026.
Its key product families include, but are not limited to, DC-to-DC, AC-to-DC, driver metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, power management IC, current-limit switch and lighting-control products.
DC to DC ICs are used to convert and control voltages within a broad range of electronic systems, such as portable electronic devices, wireless LAN access points, computers and monitors, automobiles and medical equipment.
Lighting control ICs are used in backlighting and general illumination products.
By end market, 38.8% of total revenues came from Enterprise Data in the second quarter of 2026.

The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.
Individual investors often find it hard to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, since these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time. In these situations, the Zacks rating system comes in handy because of the power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements.

Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, has proven to be strongly correlated with the near-term price movement of its stock. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
Fundamentally speaking, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade for Monolithic imply an improvement in the company's underlying business. Investors should show their appreciation for this improving business trend by pushing the stock higher.

Here's What to Expect From Monolithic Power Systems' Next Earnings Report
Monolithic Power Systems (MPS) logo_By Rafael Henrique
West Palm Beach, Florida-based Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (MPWR) provides semiconductor-based power electronics solutions in the United States and internationally. The company has a market cap of $64.8 billion and offers direct current (DC) to DC solutions to convert and control voltages within a range of electronic systems, including cloud-based and on-premises CPU servers and workstations, AI systems, memory, storage solutions, and more.
MPWR is expected to release its Q3 2026 earnings on Thursday, October 29, after the market closes. SCHAFFHAUSEN, Switzerland, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (MPS) (Nasdaq: MPWR), a fabless global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions, today announced it will report its third quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, October 29, 2026 after the market closes. MPS will host a question-and-answer webinar at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET on the same day to discuss the results and business outlook.
The webinar can be accessed from the Investor Relations section of the MPS website at www.monolithicpower.com. A replay of the event will be available on the website for one year.
About Monolithic Power Systems, Inc.
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (“MPS”) is a fabless global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions. MPS’s mission is to reduce energy and material consumption to improve all aspects of quality of life and create a sustainable future. Founded in 1997 by our CEO Michael Hsing, MPS has three core strengths: deep system-level knowledge, strong semiconductor design expertise, and innovative proprietary technologies in the areas of semiconductor processes, system integration, and packaging. These combined advantages enable MPS to deliver reliable, compact, and monolithic solutions that are highly energy-efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible while providing a consistent return on investment to our stockholders. MPS can be contacted through its website at www.monolithicpower.com or its support offices around the world.

Here's How Much You'd Have If You Invested $1000 in Monolithic Power a Decade Ago
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:30 AM CDT 3 min read
For most investors, how much a stock's price changes over time is important. This factor can impact your investment portfolio as well as help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.
The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.
What if you'd invested in Monolithic Power (MPWR) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to MPWR for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?
With that in mind, let's take a look at Monolithic Power's main business drivers.
Monolithic Power Systems, based in Kirkland, WA, designs, develops and markets high-performance power solutions. The company focuses on the market for high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs).
Monolithic's products are widely used in industrial applications, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud computing, and automotive and consumer applications.
Being a fabless company, Monolithic works with third-party contractors and chip assemblers for the manufacturing, assembling and testing of wafers and ICs. This approach permits the company to focus more on the designing and development of process technology at a lower fixed cost.
Unlike other fabless semiconductor companies, Monolithic installs its own proprietary process technologies in third-party contractors' equipment and facilities.
Monolithic reported total revenues of $980.6 million in the second quarter of 2026.
Its key product families include, but are not limited to, DC-to-DC, AC-to-DC, driver metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, power management IC, current-limit switch and lighting-control products.
DC to DC ICs are used to convert and control voltages within a broad range of electronic systems, such as portable electronic devices, wireless LAN access points, computers and monitors, automobiles and medical equipment.
Lighting control ICs are used in backlighting and general illumination products.
By end market, 38.8% of total revenues came from Enterprise Data in the second quarter of 2026.
Storage and Computing, Consumer, Industrial, Automotive and Communications end-markets contributed 20.4%, 5.8%, 5.6%, 16.0% and 13.4%, respectively, to the second quarter of 2026 revenues.
Monolithic's primary competitors are Analog Devices, Infineon Technologies, NXP Semiconductors, ON Semiconductor, Power Integrations, Renesas Electronics, ROHM Semiconductor, Semtech, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments.
While anyone can invest, building a lucrative investment portfolio takes research, patience, and a little bit of risk. If you had invested in Monolithic Power ten years ago, you're probably feeling pretty good about your investment today.
A $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $16,187.64, or a gain of 1,518.76%, as of October 16, 2026, according to our calculations. This return excludes dividends but includes price appreciation.
The S&P 500 rose 263.06% and the price of gold increased 220.64% over the same time frame in comparison.
Analysts are forecasting more upside for MPWR too.
Monolithic is benefiting from expanding power content across AI infrastructure, enterprise data and communications as customers adopt higher-density designs and module solutions. New customer ramps, platform refreshes and DDR5 orders expand its market, while sampling for 800-volt data-center architectures adds a growth avenue. Automotive design wins, robotics activity and building automation extend opportunities beyond core power-management products, while the GlobalFoundries partnership should add capacity and diversify supply from 2027. However, semiconductor cyclicality, high data-center exposure and gross margins near the low end of management's model temper the outlook. Geopolitical uncertainty, execution risk in emerging applications and a premium valuation further limit upside, supporting a balanced view.
Shares have gained 6.81% over the past four weeks and there have been 2 higher earnings estimate revisions for fiscal 2026 compared to none lower. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

Monolithic (MPWR) Upgraded to Buy: What Does It Mean for the Stock?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Monolithic Power (MPWR) could be a solid choice for investors given its recent upgrade to a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). An upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices -- has triggered this rating change.
The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.
Individual investors often find it hard to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, since these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time. In these situations, the Zacks rating system comes in handy because of the power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements.
As such, the Zacks rating upgrade for Monolithic is essentially a positive comment on its earnings outlook that could have a favorable impact on its stock price.
Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, has proven to be strongly correlated with the near-term price movement of its stock. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
Fundamentally speaking, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade for Monolithic imply an improvement in the company's underlying business. Investors should show their appreciation for this improving business trend by pushing the stock higher.
Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions
As empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock movements, tracking such revisions for making an investment decision could be truly rewarding. Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.
The Zacks Rank stock-rating system, which uses four factors related to earnings estimates to classify stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), has an impressive externally-audited track record, with Zacks Rank #1 stocks generating an average annual return of +25% since 1988. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Earnings Estimate Revisions for Monolithic
This chipmaker is expected to earn $27.48 per share for the fiscal year ending December 2026, which represents no year-over-year change.
Analysts have been steadily raising their estimates for Monolithic. Over the past three months, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company has increased 17.5%.
Unlike the overly optimistic Wall Street analysts whose rating systems tend to be weighted toward favorable recommendations, the Zacks rating system maintains an equal proportion of "buy" and "sell" ratings for its entire universe of more than 4,000 stocks at any point in time. Irrespective of market conditions, only the top 5% of the Zacks-covered stocks get a "Strong Buy" rating and the next 15% get a "Buy" rating. So, the placement of a stock in the top 20% of the Zacks-covered stocks indicates its superior earnings estimate revision feature, making it a solid candidate for producing market-beating returns in the near term.

Monolithic Power Systems, MACOM, Micron, Seagate, and Vishay Intertechnology Shares Plummet, What You Need To Know
What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after worries weighed on memory chipmakers and sparked selling pressure across the broader semiconductor sector, following news of domestic Chinese technological advancements and looming labor strikes in Taiwan.
As detailed by TipRanks, Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced significant progress on a next-generation 4F² DRAM server-memory design due by late 2026, launching denser DDR5 enterprise server modules that directly rival architectures currently being developed by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
However, the financial research firm added that CXMT has yet to prove it can manufacture the chips in commercial volumes. Amplifying the negative sentiment, Reuters, via Investing.com, reported that escalating labor tension in Taiwan added direct pressure on Micron, as 1,994 Taoyuan union members—representing 99% of ballots cast—voted to authorize a strike seeking a permanent 15% profit-sharing bonus. Investing.com noted that these Taiwan sites house 15,000 workers and anchor Micron's critical DRAM and high-bandwidth memory output, though no strike date has been set.
Consequently, shares of major memory manufacturers, including Micron, SanDisk, and SK Hynix, pulled back in early trade as these regional supply chain threats rattled investors. According to financial media, the widespread selling also dragged down the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which declined 1% during premarket activity.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming In On Vishay Intertechnology (VSH)
Vishay Intertechnology's shares are extremely volatile and have had 53 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 10 days ago when the stock gained 11.1% on the news that the company released four new power modules equipped with 650 V superjunction MOSFETs in standard SOT-227 packaging, while simultaneously benefiting from a sector-wide rally driven by cooling Treasury yields.
As detailed in the corporate announcement, the new modules feature single-switch configurations with ratings of 50 A, 100 A, and 150 A, as well as a 50 A low-side chopper configuration integrating a 650 V silicon carbide diode. The firm noted that these components are built for high-efficiency power conversion, targeting industrial applications such as solar inverters, charging stations, and medical imaging systems, while functioning as drop-in replacements that eliminate the need for customers to redesign printed circuit boards.
According to CNBC, this product launch was amplified by favorable macroeconomic tailwinds after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that September nonfarm payrolls increased by only 29,000—falling significantly short of the 84,000 projected by economists polled by Dow Jones—while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. CNBC observed that this softer hiring data eased interest-rate pressure on high-multiple growth equities by pulling borrowing costs lower. Consequently, market commentators noted that semiconductor valuations expand when falling yields reduce the discount rate on long-duration earnings, provided that enterprise infrastructure spending holds and further labor deceleration does not dampen cyclical industrial and automotive chip channels.
Vishay Intertechnology is up 106% since the beginning of the year, but at $31.56 per share, it is still trading 51.4% below its 52-week high of $64.90 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Vishay Intertechnology's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,651.

Monolithic Power’s Margin Jump Came Below Gross Profit. Why That Matters for the Next Downturn
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:MPWR) lifted its second-quarter operating margin to 31% from 24.8%, while gross margin barely changed. The improvement shows how quickly revenue growth can lift earnings when operating expenses rise more slowly. It also identifies a source of downside if semiconductor demand weakens.
In the July 30 results, revenue increased 47.6% to $980.6 million. GAAP gross margin was 55.2%, compared with 55.1% a year earlier, while operating expenses increased 17.8% to $237.2 million. The company spread those expenses across a much larger sales base.
Broadcom’s $29 Billion AI Backstop: How Much Risk Does the Cash Flow Cover?
Monolithic Power ranked sixth in our October 6 long-term performance list. Find which five stocks compounded faster over the measured 20-year period, and where other chip businesses finished.
The same cost structure works in both directions
Holding quarterly operating expenses at $237.2 million and gross margin at 55.2%, a 10% revenue decline from the second-quarter level would leave $250.0 million of operating profit. The resulting margin would be 28.3%. This simplified sensitivity excludes any cost response or mix change.
Further growth can support disproportionate profit gains; a sales setback can compress margins even without worse pricing. The model retains GAAP costs, including $53.5 million of stock compensation and related expenses.
Find the AI power-content opportunity behind Monolithic Power's growth, and the demand test that could undermine it.
There is room for a revenue retreat before the previous year's operating margin returns, but the buffer is finite. With the same gross margin and expenses, quarterly sales of about $780 million would produce a 24.8% operating margin. That is 20% below the current quarter. If competitive pricing also reduced gross margin, the old profitability level would return sooner.
Revenue quality must support the profit gain
Inventory increased sequentially to $675.8 million from $619.2 million, although inventory days fell. Faster turnover alongside a larger inventory balance is consistent with supporting growth, but neither measure rules out a later customer slowdown.
Operating cash flow of $227.9 million was below the previous quarter's $250.3 million despite stronger sales. Inventory and receivables require funding as the business scales, so accounting operating leverage does not guarantee equally fast cash growth. A later inventory correction could pressure both sales and the cash tied up in unsold components.
Our Micron analysis tests how much financial protection a chip supplier really has when customer demand and investment spending move against it.
The stock closed October 8 at $1,369.80, equivalent to 65.6 times four times second-quarter GAAP EPS of $5.22. Annualizing one quarter is a reference point, not a full-year forecast or fair-value estimate.
Growing into the valuation requires financing inventory and receivables while retaining the expense discipline that lifted margins. If sales stall, reverse operating leverage could reduce earnings faster than revenue, making the current profit base a poor floor for a valuation model.

Monolithic Power Systems to Report Third Quarter 2026 Results on October 29, 2026
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc.
Monolithic Power Systems to Report Third Quarter 2026 Results on October 29, 2026 · globenewswire.com
SCHAFFHAUSEN, Switzerland, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (MPS) (Nasdaq: MPWR), a fabless global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions, today announced it will report its third quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, October 29, 2026 after the market closes. MPS will host a question-and-answer webinar at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET on the same day to discuss the results and business outlook.
The webinar can be accessed from the Investor Relations section of the MPS website at www.monolithicpower.com. A replay of the event will be available on the website for one year.
About Monolithic Power Systems, Inc.
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. ("MPS") is a fabless global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions. MPS's mission is to reduce energy and material consumption to improve all aspects of quality of life and create a sustainable future. Founded in 1997 by our CEO Michael Hsing, MPS has three core strengths: deep system-level knowledge, strong semiconductor design expertise, and innovative proprietary technologies in the areas of semiconductor processes, system integration, and packaging. These combined advantages enable MPS to deliver reliable, compact, and monolithic solutions that are highly energy-efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible while providing a consistent return on investment to our stockholders. MPS can be contacted through its website at www.monolithicpower.com or its support offices around the world.
Monolithic Power Systems, MPS, and the MPS logo are registered trademarks of Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. in the U.S. and trademarked in certain other countries.

Here's What to Expect From Monolithic Power Systems' Next Earnings Report
Monolithic Power Systems (MPS) logo_By Rafael Henrique
West Palm Beach, Florida-based Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (MPWR) provides semiconductor-based power electronics solutions in the United States and internationally. The company has a market cap of $64.8 billion and offers direct current (DC) to DC solutions to convert and control voltages within a range of electronic systems, including cloud-based and on-premises CPU servers and workstations, AI systems, memory, storage solutions, and more.
MPWR is expected to release its Q3 2026 earnings on Thursday, October 29, after the market closes. Ahead of the event, analysts expect the company's EPS to be $6.53 on a diluted basis, up 75.5% from $3.72 in the year-ago quarter. The company has exceeded Wall Street's EPS estimates in three of its last four quarters, while missing on one occasion.

For fiscal 2026, analysts project the company's EPS to be $23.32, up 82.3% from $12.79 in fiscal 2025. Moreover, its EPS is expected to rise by roughly 30.5% year over year (YoY) to $30.43 in fiscal 2027.
Monolithic Power shares have surged 32.2% over the past 52 weeks, rallying the S&P 500 Index's ($SPX) 19.2% rise but lagging behind the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF's (XLK) 41.1% rise during the same time frame.
On Sept. 1, MPWR stock declined 3.3% after crude oil prices surged, accompanied by a jump in benchmark Treasury yields. The rising prices brought up concerns over inflation and prolonged corporate borrowing costs. Following several U.S. military strikes in Iran, and news of new strikes also being on the horizon, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 4.79%, marking a 20-month high. Geopolitical tension leading to higher energy and logistics costs ultimately led to concern over tightening margins across global chip supply chains.
Analysts are also highly optimistic about MPWR, with the stock having a "Strong Buy" rating overall. Among the 14 analysts covering the stock, 10 recommend a "Strong Buy," two recommend a "Moderate Buy," and two recommend a "Hold." MPWR's average analyst price target of $1,822.25 offers a 38.1% upside potential.

Monolithic Power Systems Announces Third Quarter 2026 Dividend
Schaffhausen, Switzerland, September 10, 2026 -- Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (“MPS”) (Nasdaq: MPWR), a global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions, announced today its third quarter dividend of $2.00 per common share to all stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 30, 2026. The dividend will be paid on October 15, 2026.
This news release includes “forward-looking statements” intended to qualify for the safe harbor from liability established by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These forward-looking statements are based on our current expectations, estimates and projections about our business and industry, management’s beliefs, and certain assumptions made by us, all of which are subject to change. Forward-looking statements can often be identified by words such as “anticipates,” “expects,” “forecasts,” “intends,” “believes,” “plans,” “may,” “will,” or “continue,” and similar expressions and variations or negatives of these words. Should one or more of these risks or uncertainties materialize, or should underlying assumptions prove incorrect, actual results may vary materially and adversely from those projected, and may affect our future operating results, financial position and cash flows. Accordingly, you are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which speak only as of the date they are made. Except to the extent required by law, MPS does not undertake, and expressly disclaims, any duty or obligation to update publicly any forward-looking statement after the initial distribution of this release, whether as a result of new information, future events, changes in assumptions or otherwise.
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (“MPS”) is a fabless global company that provides high-performance, semiconductor-based power electronics solutions. MPS’s mission is to reduce energy and material consumption to improve all aspects of quality of life and create a sustainable future. Founded in 1997 by our CEO Michael Hsing, MPS has three core strengths: deep system-level knowledge, strong semiconductor design expertise, and innovative proprietary technologies in the areas of semiconductor processes, system integration, and packaging. These combined advantages enable MPS to deliver reliable, compact, and monolithic solutions that are highly energy-efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible while providing a consistent return on investment to our stockholders. MPS can be contacted through its website at www.monolithicpower.com or its support offices around the world.

COLUMBUS, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 20, 2026--
Accenture (NYSE: ACN), Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities. These utilities provide essential services but often lack resources for adequate protection for their operational technology (OT) environments. The announcement comes amid a recent surge in cyberattacks targeting more than 100 U.S. water systems across over a dozen states.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261020093364/en/
Accenture, Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities.
In its first phase, the initiative will provide cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training free of charge to up to 500 under-resourced utilities. Accenture, Dragos and SANS are making an initial combined commitment of approximately $10 million in funding and services. In addition, Elastic is supporting the initiative through technology that allows for software delivery at scale by providing the primary log storage and query engine within the Dragos Platform.
Many of the tens of thousands of small utilities across the U.S., particularly those serving rural or underserved communities, face limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology. This leaves the pumps, valves, substations and distribution networks that support essential services vulnerable to cyberattacks that can threaten public safety.
To address this gap, Accenture, Dragos and SANS are launching the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to provide eligible utilities with OT cybersecurity technology, deployment support, hardware and training. The initiative builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which provides more than 100 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform. The foundation was announced at a roundtable discussion focused on strengthening the cybersecurity of utilities in Ohio, hosted by American Electric Power (AEP) subsidiary Ohio Power Company, Accenture and Dragos.
“Our work with America’s critical infrastructure operators has shown both the gravity of the cyber threats they face and a widening vulnerability gap—between large operators with the resources to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack those means,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “Together with Dragos and SANS, we will provide under-resourced utilities with the technology, expertise and training they need to better power and protect the communities they serve.”
“Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats,” said Robert M. Lee, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of Dragos. “The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost.”
Who qualifies, how to apply Eligible participants include U.S. based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue. More than 97% of utilities fall below this threshold, representing more than 50,000 organizations that may need support. Participants can expect:
Access to the Dragos Platform and services to help organizations know what’s on their networks and how to address vulnerabilities and threats. Elasticsearch provides the underlying log storage and search capabilities that help Dragos deliver the platform at scale to participating utilities.
Accenture deployment services including expert configuration, integration and ongoing support.
SANS ICS/OT training to build and sustain in-house capabilities.
Hardware and infrastructurefunding to purchase the equipment needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform.
Peer community access connecting participants to a network of utilities sharing operational experience.
“ The best security technology in the world won’t protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on,” said James Lyne, CEO, SANS.
“Strong cybersecurity depends on many technologies working together. Elastic is committed to supporting Dragos in delivering its platform at scale, helping make advanced cybersecurity capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them,” said Ashutosh Kulkarni, CEO, Elastic.
Utilities interested in participating can learn more at https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
About the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation is a nonprofit launched by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute. It raises and provides the funding, hardware, deployment services, and training that small, under-resourced utilities in the U.S. need to secure their operational technology environments. Visit https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.

Dragos serves critical sectors such as energy, manufacturing, water, transportation, data centers, mining, and ports. Credit: Tobias Arhelger via Shutterstock
Accenture is exploring a sale of its Greater China business, in a deal that could value the unit at up to $1.5bn, the Financial Times reported on Sunday.
The consulting firm has hired JPMorgan to run a strategic review of the unit, according to the Financial Times report, which cited people familiar with the matter. The review follows unsolicited interest in the business over the past year, the paper said.
Accenture and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters, which were sent outside regular business hours.
The Greater China unit covers mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, according to Accenture’s website. Its wider Asia-Pacific business brought in about $10bn in revenue last year, the FT said.
A sale would probably draw private equity groups and a small number of strategic buyers, the FT reported. Accenture could also keep a significant minority stake to give clients continuity. However, there is no certainty that the review will lead to a deal.
The FT also pointed to wider pressure on Western advisers in China. Several, including McKinsey, have scaled back there. At the same time, tighter Chinese security rules limit how much sensitive data can leave the country.
Accenture has already signalled that it is willing to sell parts of the company. At a recent investor event, chief financial officer Angie Park said it can raise money by selling assets, according to the FT.
The firm has a record of “exiting businesses, offerings, countries, contracts that no longer meet our strategic or return thresholds,” Park said, according to the FT.
The report comes as Accenture tries to convince investors that AI will bring it more work, not less. Some investors fear AI could let clients bring work in-house, the FT said. In June, its shares suffered their worst one-day drop on record after a weak forecast.
The stock then rose by about a fifth on October 1, after fourth-quarter results beat expectations. Revenue for the year to August rose 6.5% to $74.2bn. For fiscal 2027, the company expects growth of 3% to 6%.
At its investor day on October 14, Accenture said it plans about $8bn of acquisitions in fiscal 2027. That figure includes its deal for industrial security firm Dragos. It also aims to return at least $9.5bn to shareholders next year.
Money from a China sale could help pay for those plans, the FT said.

Accenture told many employees in an internal memo, reported on October 15, 2026, that it will pay only that fixed monthly amount toward Claude, the AI model built by privately held Anthropic. Anything above it must be charged to a project.
Accenture sells AI transformation to roughly 9,000 clients. Internally, it now limits spending on the same tools.

What Accenture’s Claude Memo Actually Commits To
The memo, titled “Claude Enterprise Users: Important Updates to Licensing and Usage Costs,” states that “all costs are consumption-based.” Usage above the allowance goes to a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), Accenture’s billing code for a project or team.
Heavy use remains possible, but it now needs a budget owner. Premium plans include $250 of weekly token usage, although many employees are not on Premium.

This is one policy, reported indirectly. Total spending, affected headcount, and whether other AI tools face similar limits remain unknown.
Accenture keeps expanding in AI, with nearly 110,000 AI and data professionals. Sweet also called the Anthropic relationship non-exclusive. For AI vendors, tight limits at the largest IT services firms could slow enterprise spending, although targeted use on proven work may last longer.

The firm also offers on-the-ground program delivery services to keep programs moving, with Avicado specialists serving as owner representatives, supporting site selection and feasibility, managing procurement services, and providing controls, schedule and document management.
Avicado serves large project owners across data centers, transportation, government and public infrastructure, commercial real estate, education, healthcare, manufacturing, power and energy, and water and wastewater. Its team of more than 190 professionals will join Accenture Construct in the United States.
“Avicado brings exceptional talent and deep expertise in the digital platforms that underpin many capital programs,” said Adam J. Shaw, CEO of Accenture Construct. “It’s our next move to give owners the full breadth of capabilities they need—proven industry platforms, people and process, and AI—and enabling us to take greater accountability for client outcomes.”
“We have a community of great people who focus on continuous improvement, and that’s what drives impact on our clients’ programs,” said Avidahn Levin, founder and CEO of Avicado. “Joining Accenture Construct lets us bring our specialist experience to more clients and programs and gives our existing clients access to Accenture’s global capabilities, industry knowledge and technology. I’m excited for our team to grow their careers at Accenture Construct.”

Accenture, Dragos and SANS Institute Launch Foundation to Strengthen Cyber Defenses for Under-Resourced U.S. Utilities
Accenture, Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities.
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 12:59 PM CDT 7 min read
Approximately $10 million in initial funding and services will support essential services relied on by more than 100 million Americans
Initiative will provide technology, deployment services and training at no cost to up to 500 under-resourced utilities
COLUMBUS, Ohio, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Accenture (NYSE: ACN), Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities. These utilities provide essential services but often lack resources for adequate protection for their operational technology (OT) environments. The announcement comes amid a recent surge in cyberattacks targeting more than 100 U.S. water systems across over a dozen states.
In its first phase, the initiative will provide cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training free of charge to up to 500 under-resourced utilities. Accenture, Dragos and SANS are making an initial combined commitment of approximately $10 million in funding and services. In addition, Elastic is supporting the initiative through technology that allows for software delivery at scale by providing the primary log storage and query engine within the Dragos Platform.
Many of the tens of thousands of small utilities across the U.S., particularly those serving rural or underserved communities, face limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology. This leaves the pumps, valves, substations and distribution networks that support essential services vulnerable to cyberattacks that can threaten public safety.
To address this gap, Accenture, Dragos and SANS are launching the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to provide eligible utilities with OT cybersecurity technology, deployment support, hardware and training. The initiative builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which provides more than 100 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform. The foundation was announced at a roundtable discussion focused on strengthening the cybersecurity of utilities in Ohio, hosted by American Electric Power (AEP) subsidiary Ohio Power Company, Accenture and Dragos.
"Our work with America's critical infrastructure operators has shown both the gravity of the cyber threats they face and a widening vulnerability gap—between large operators with the resources to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack those means," said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. "Together with Dragos and SANS, we will provide under-resourced utilities with the technology, expertise and training they need to better power and protect the communities they serve."
"Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats," said Robert M. Lee, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of Dragos. "The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost."
Eligible participants include U.S. based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue. More than 97% of utilities fall below this threshold, representing more than 50,000 organizations that may need support. Participants can expect:
Access to the Dragos Platform and services to help organizations know what's on their networks and how to address vulnerabilities and threats. Elasticsearch provides the underlying log storage and search capabilities that help Dragos deliver the platform at scale to participating utilities.
Accenture deployment services including expert configuration, integration and ongoing support.
SANS ICS/OT training to build and sustain in-house capabilities.
Hardware and infrastructure funding to purchase the equipment needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform.
Peer community access connecting participants to a network of utilities sharing operational experience.
"The best security technology in the world won't protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on," said James Lyne, CEO, SANS.
"Strong cybersecurity depends on many technologies working together. Elastic is committed to supporting Dragos in delivering its platform at scale, helping make advanced cybersecurity capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them," said Ashutosh Kulkarni, CEO, Elastic.
Utilities interested in participating can learn more at https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
About the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation
The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation is a nonprofit launched by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute. It raises and provides the funding, hardware, deployment services, and training that small, under-resourced utilities in the U.S. need to secure their operational technology environments. Visit https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.

This initiative, which builds on the recent announcement of Accenture's Gemini Enterprise Business Group (part of the Accenture Google Business Group), provides federal agencies with a centralized hub of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to industrialize how they build, deploy, and scale enterprise agents. By embedding these specialized FDEs alongside agencies, the government can focus on delivering outcome-based, high-code agents built on Gemini, that integrate directly into core government systems of record and enable practitioners to execute complex workflows.
By activating a Gemini launchpad, agencies can centrally manage the agent–from securely connecting Gemini to mission datasets and prioritizing agent use cases to rapid deployment and workforce training. This provides leadership with a single view to track performance, measure mission impact, and drive even more value from their investment in Gemini.
"The real opportunity to scale value for our clients is deploying these purpose-built agents to transform work at the heart of government operations," said Ron Ash, CEO of Accenture Federal Services. This collaboration further moves governments beyond incremental modernization—equipping public servants with intelligent capabilities to navigate complex systems, accelerate critical decisions, and deliver at the speed of mission."
Accelerating Mission Impact with Specialized Engineers and Pre-Built Agents
To meet federal demand and accelerate this mission, Accenture Federal Services is training an initial cohort of Google Cloud- skilled FDEs. This training would be part of Accenture's recently announced commitment to establish a 1,000-person FDE workforce Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group.
These FDEs will embed directly alongside agency teams and Accenture Federal's functional subject matter experts to bridge the gap between technology and mission. COLUMBUS, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 20, 2026--
Accenture (NYSE: ACN), Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities. These utilities provide essential services but often lack resources for adequate protection for their operational technology (OT) environments. The announcement comes amid a recent surge in cyberattacks targeting more than 100 U.S. water systems across over a dozen states.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261020093364/en/
Accenture, Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities.
In its first phase, the initiative will provide cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training free of charge to up to 500 under-resourced utilities. Accenture, Dragos and SANS are making an initial combined commitment of approximately $10 million in funding and services. In addition, Elastic is supporting the initiative through technology that allows for software delivery at scale by providing the primary log storage and query engine within the Dragos Platform.
Many of the tens of thousands of small utilities across the U.S., particularly those serving rural or underserved communities, face limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology. This leaves the pumps, valves, substations and distribution networks that support essential services vulnerable to cyberattacks that can threaten public safety.
To address this gap, Accenture, Dragos and SANS are launching the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to provide eligible utilities with OT cybersecurity technology, deployment support, hardware and training. The initiative builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which provides more than 100 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform. The foundation was announced at a roundtable discussion focused on strengthening the cybersecurity of utilities in Ohio, hosted by American Electric Power (AEP) subsidiary Ohio Power Company, Accenture and Dragos.
“Our work with America’s critical infrastructure operators has shown both the gravity of the cyber threats they face and a widening vulnerability gap—between large operators with the resources to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack those means,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “Together with Dragos and SANS, we will provide under-resourced utilities with the technology, expertise and training they need to better power and protect the communities they serve.”
“Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats,” said Robert M. Lee, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of Dragos. “The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost.”
Who qualifies, how to apply Eligible participants include U.S. based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue. More than 97% of utilities fall below this threshold, representing more than 50,000 organizations that may need support. Participants can expect:
Access to the Dragos Platform and services to help organizations know what’s on their networks and how to address vulnerabilities and threats. Elasticsearch provides the underlying log storage and search capabilities that help Dragos deliver the platform at scale to participating utilities.
Accenture deployment services including expert configuration, integration and ongoing support.
SANS ICS/OT training to build and sustain in-house capabilities.
Hardware and infrastructurefunding to purchase the equipment needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform.
Peer community access connecting participants to a network of utilities sharing operational experience.
“ The best security technology in the world won’t protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on,” said James Lyne, CEO, SANS.
“Strong cybersecurity depends on many technologies working together. Elastic is committed to supporting Dragos in delivering its platform at scale, helping make advanced cybersecurity capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them,” said Ashutosh Kulkarni, CEO, Elastic.
Utilities interested in participating can learn more at https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
About the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation is a nonprofit launched by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute. It raises and provides the funding, hardware, deployment services, and training that small, under-resourced utilities in the U.S. need to secure their operational technology environments. Visit https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
About Accenture Accenture is a business reinvention and technology company. Our ambition is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. Our approximately 814,000 people bring deep insights across industries and functions, with capabilities spanning strategy, process, operating model, change management, talent, data, technology and AI. We deliver this expertise through consulting, managed services, proprietary assets and platforms, and increasingly, software. We bring innovation and new solutions informed by our experience across industries, enabling us to apply relevant insights, capabilities and leading practices from adjacent sectors to address emerging business challenges and opportunities. We serve more than 9,000 clients and generated revenues of approximately $74 billion in fiscal year 2026. Visit us at accenture.com.
About Dragos Dragos is the global leader in extended operational technology (xOT) cybersecurity, delivering on its mission to safeguard civilization. The Dragos Platform delivers asset visibility, continuous monitoring, OT vulnerability management, segmentation validation, device protection, and real-time threat detection, powered by the industry’s most experienced OT threat intelligence and incident response team. Dragos serves critical sectors such as energy, manufacturing, water, transportation, data centers, mining, and ports. Privately held and headquartered in the Washington, DC area, Dragos operates globally across North America, EMEA, and APAC. Visit dragos.com.
About SANS Institute The SANS Institute was established in 1989 as a cooperative research and education organization. Today, SANS is the most trusted and, by far, the largest provider of cybersecurity training and certification to professionals in government and commercial institutions worldwide. Renowned SANS instructors teach more than 85 courses at in-person and virtual cybersecurity events and OnDemand. GIAC, an affiliate of the SANS Institute, validates practitioner skills through more than 50 hands-on technical certifications in cybersecurity.

Credit: Tobias Arhelger via Shutterstock
Accenture is exploring a sale of its Greater China business, in a deal that could value the unit at up to $1.5bn, the Financial Times reported on Sunday.
The consulting firm has hired JPMorgan to run a strategic review of the unit, according to the Financial Times report, which cited people familiar with the matter. The review follows unsolicited interest in the business over the past year, the paper said.
Accenture and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters, which were sent outside regular business hours.
The Greater China unit covers mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, according to Accenture’s website. Its wider Asia-Pacific business brought in about $10bn in revenue last year, the FT said.
A sale would probably draw private equity groups and a small number of strategic buyers, the FT reported. Accenture could also keep a significant minority stake to give clients continuity. However, there is no certainty that the review will lead to a deal.
The FT also pointed to wider pressure on Western advisers in China. Several, including McKinsey, have scaled back there. At the same time, tighter Chinese security rules limit how much sensitive data can leave the country.
Accenture has already signalled that it is willing to sell parts of the company. At a recent investor event, chief financial officer Angie Park said it can raise money by selling assets, according to the FT.
The firm has a record of “exiting businesses, offerings, countries, contracts that no longer meet our strategic or return thresholds,” Park said, according to the FT.
The report comes as Accenture tries to convince investors that AI will bring it more work, not less. Some investors fear AI could let clients bring work in-house, the FT said. In June, its shares suffered their worst one-day drop on record after a weak forecast.
The stock then rose by about a fifth on October 1, after fourth-quarter results beat expectations. Revenue for the year to August rose 6.5% to $74.2bn. For fiscal 2027, the company expects growth of 3% to 6%.
At its investor day on October 14, Accenture said it plans about $8bn of acquisitions in fiscal 2027. That figure includes its deal for industrial security firm Dragos. It also aims to return at least $9.5bn to shareholders next year.
Money from a China sale could help pay for those plans, the FT said.

Accenture Just Capped Employees’ Claude Spending at $29 a Month. Some Were Spending $1,000
Accenture sells AI transformation to thousands of clients while quietly telling its own employees they get a fraction of what some were already spending. The internal memo reveals a tension at the heart of every major consulting firm racing to…
Published October 16, 2026, 9:27am ET · 3 min read
A businessman engages in strategic planning amidst a backdrop of global AI innovation and financial data. The image underscores the intricate balance between technological advancement and sound personal finance in the rapidly evolving digital landscape. © MUNGKHOOD STUDIO / Shutterstock.com
An Accenture (NYSE:ACN | ACN Price Prediction) consultant building an AI solution for several clients said Claude Code usage ran between $500 and $1,000 a month. Starting October 1, the company will centrally fund $29 per person.
Accenture told many employees in an internal memo, reported on October 15, 2026, that it will pay only that fixed monthly amount toward Claude, the AI model built by privately held Anthropic. Anything above it must be charged to a project.
Accenture sells AI transformation to roughly 9,000 clients. Internally, it now limits spending on the same tools.
Shares rose 4.63% to $224.92 on October 15 during a broad software rally unrelated to the memo, yet they remain well below the 52-week high of $291.09.
What Accenture’s Claude Memo Actually Commits To
The memo, titled “Claude Enterprise Users: Important Updates to Licensing and Usage Costs,” states that “all costs are consumption-based.” Usage above the allowance goes to a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), Accenture’s billing code for a project or team.
Heavy use remains possible, but it now needs a budget owner. Premium plans include $250 of weekly token usage, although many employees are not on Premium.
Access is conditional. The memo says, “Providing a WBS and obtaining a license does not guarantee indefinite or ongoing access to Claude,” and one employee lost access entirely.
Accenture did not publish the memo or say how many employees are affected. A spokesperson said, “Our approach today is to provide the right tool for the right work.”
Consumption Billing Shows What Coding AI Really Costs
The $29 cap targets a consumer subscription price point. Agentic coding tools, which carry out complex tasks on their own, consume far more tokens, the units AI models bill by.
One employee said usage topped $500 a month for months, and some spent as much as $1,000. Per-seat budgets are likely to fall short once work shifts to autonomous coding.
CEO Julie Sweet said on the October 1 earnings call that falling token costs will “enable companies to use AI in more places and at scale.” The memo suggests that prices likely have further to fall before agentic coding becomes cheap enough to fund on a per-seat basis.
Accenture earns its margin on labor across roughly 814,000 employees. Unlimited token spending on that base is a cost that grows without a matching revenue line.
Charging overruns to a WBS ties AI spending to client work. Fixed-price work is over 65% of bookings, so AI costs on those contracts land on Accenture unless they were priced in.
Management guided to a 15.9% to 16.1% operating margin for fiscal 2027, which leaves little room for unmanaged expense.
This is one policy, reported indirectly. Total spending, affected headcount, and whether other AI tools face similar limits remain unknown.
Accenture keeps expanding in AI, with nearly 110,000 AI and data professionals. Sweet also called the Anthropic relationship non-exclusive. For AI vendors, tight limits at the largest IT services firms could slow enterprise spending, although targeted use on proven work may last longer.
What Cost Discipline Means for Accenture’s Fiscal 2027 Outlook
The memo shows cost discipline that supports fiscal 2027 guidance for GAAP EPS of $14.39 to $14.81.
The gap from the 52-week high, with market value at $134.05 billion, reflects fears that AI will reduce IT services billing. A record 141 quarterly bookings of $100 million or more argue demand is holding.
The thesis fails if management says at the next earnings report that AI tool costs are pressuring margins, or if first-quarter revenue lands below the $18.95 billion low end of guidance.

Accenture Expands Federal AI Push With Google's Gemini Agents, Months After OpenAI Partnership
The companies are targeting government workflows with embedded AI engineers and pre-built agents, but have not disclosed contract values or named federal customers.
Accenture store is seen at Promenade Street in Davos, Switzerland on January 21, 2025. (Photo by Ömer Sercan Karku/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Accenture plans to train an initial group of Google Cloud-skilled engineers as part of its broader 1,000-person engineering workforce initiative.
The companies are developing pre-built AI agents for human resources, finance and supply chain operations.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Accenture (ACN) and Google Public Sector announced on Monday the deployment of Gemini launchpads, a new capability designed to help U.S. federal agencies move artificial intelligence (AI) agents beyond experimentation and into government operations.
The initiative pairs Google's (GOOG, GOOGL) Gemini technology with Accenture Federal Services' engineering expertise to build agents that can integrate with existing government systems and handle complex workflows.

The launchpads will provide federal agencies with a centralized team of forward-deployed engineers who will work alongside government personnel to develop and deploy customized AI agents.
Accenture said agencies will be able to connect Gemini to government datasets, identify potential applications, manage deployments and train employees through a centralized platform. Agency leaders will also be able to monitor agent performance and assess operational outcomes.

The companies are developing pre-built agents for functions such as human resources, finance and supply chain management, targeting routine administrative work and data-gathering tasks.
Accenture Federal Services CEO Ron Ash said embedding engineers alongside agency teams would help address operational challenges and move AI applications into core government functions.
Accenture's 1,000-Engineer AI Push Takes Shape
The announcement builds on the Gemini Enterprise Business Group, established by Accenture and Google Cloud in September.

As part of that broader initiative, Accenture committed to establishing a workforce of 1,000 forward-deployed engineers to help enterprise customers deploy Gemini-based AI applications.
Accenture Federal Services is now training an initial cohort of Google Cloud-skilled engineers under the initiative, although it did not specify how many would focus on federal agencies.
The latest move also follows Accenture Federal's May partnership with OpenAI, which similarly focused on helping federal agencies deploy AI across government operations.
Federal agencies can also participate in hands-on workshops at Accenture's The Forge facility in Washington, D.C., where the companies will demonstrate agents and help identify potential applications.

Accenture (ACN) Stock: Climbs as Avicado Acquisition Expands Digital Construction
Accenture expands its digital construction capabilities through Avicado acquisition, adding over 190 specialists and strengthening infrastructure services.
By Yasmin WernerOctober 20, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
Accenture (ACN) gains 0.72% to $238.63 as Avicado acquisition boosts services
Avicado adds more than 190 specialists to Accenture’s construction business
Accenture gains expertise across Procore, Autodesk, Trimble and Oracle tools
Acquisition expands Accenture’s reach in data centers and major infrastructure
Accenture leaves Avicado’s deal price undisclosed as it grows project services
Accenture plc acquired Miami-based Avicado to expand its digital construction services for major capital projects. Accenture (ACN) stock climbed 0.72% to $238.63, gaining $1.70 after reversing earlier losses. The acquisition strengthens Accenture Construct’s software integration and project management services across complex infrastructure developments.
Accenture Expands Digital Construction Consulting Capabilities
Accenture Construct will absorb Avicado’s consulting operations, widening its support for infrastructure owners and developers. The acquisition adds expertise in connecting construction software, improving project controls, and organizing complex workflows. As a result, project owners can manage data more efficiently and reduce manual handoffs between teams.
Avicado began operations in 2015 and maintains its headquarters in Miami, Florida. The consultancy helps organizations connect construction platforms and improve reporting throughout major projects. Its approach combines technology implementation with operational support for clients managing complex construction programs.
More than 190 Avicado employees will join Accenture Construct’s United States team. Their experience strengthens the unit’s ability to manage digital systems and construction delivery requirements. Accenture plans to combine these capabilities with its existing industry expertise and artificial intelligence services.
Avicado Brings Construction Software and Project Management Expertise
Avicado works with major construction software providers, including Procore, Autodesk, Trimble, Oracle and Kahua. The firm implements Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Oracle Primavera P6, and Textura. Its specialists also support Trimble’s e-Builder platform and integrate software across project workflows.
Beyond software implementation, Avicado assists project owners with planning and daily program delivery. Its specialists handle feasibility reviews, site selection, procurement, scheduling, and document management. They act as owner representatives and help oversee work across multiple project teams.
Avicado serves data center operators, transportation agencies, government bodies, and commercial property developers. Its customers also span education, healthcare, manufacturing, energy, water, and wastewater sectors. These industries require extensive planning, project controls, and reliable records throughout construction.
Accenture Strengthens Infrastructure Services Through Avicado Acquisition
The acquisition expands Accenture Construct’s ability to support complex capital programs across several industries. By adding Avicado’s specialists, Accenture gains deeper expertise in construction platforms and project delivery. The combination also supports its strategy of connecting technology, operational processes, and project management services.
The deal strengthens Accenture’s position in digital consulting for infrastructure development. Avicado’s experience with major construction platforms complements Accenture’s broader technology and systems integration capabilities. These services can help project owners improve coordination, manage information, and strengthen operational oversight.
Accenture did not disclose the acquisition price or provide specific financial projections for the transaction. Consequently, the deal’s direct contribution to revenue and earnings remains unclear. Nevertheless, the acquisition broadens Accenture’s construction consulting capabilities and extends its reach across capital-intensive industries.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261020697292/en/
Digital-native construction consulting firm Avicado joins Accenture Construct to expand digital and systems consulting capabilities for capital projects owners.
Founded in 2015, Avicado helps clients improve project delivery through connected systems, stronger project controls and better use of data. The digital-native company specializes in implementing and integrating leading construction and project management software from Procore, Autodesk (Construction Cloud, BIM 360), Trimble (Trimble Unity construct/e-builder), Oracle (Primavera P6, Textura) and Kahua.
The firm also offers on-the-ground program delivery services to keep programs moving, with Avicado specialists serving as owner representatives, supporting site selection and feasibility, managing procurement services, and providing controls, schedule and document management.
Avicado serves large project owners across data centers, transportation, government and public infrastructure, commercial real estate, education, healthcare, manufacturing, power and energy, and water and wastewater. Its team of more than 190 professionals will join Accenture Construct in the United States.
“Avicado brings exceptional talent and deep expertise in the digital platforms that underpin many capital programs,” said Adam J. Shaw, CEO of Accenture Construct. “It’s our next move to give owners the full breadth of capabilities they need—proven industry platforms, people and process, and AI—and enabling us to take greater accountability for client outcomes.”
“We have a community of great people who focus on continuous improvement, and that’s what drives impact on our clients’ programs,” said Avidahn Levin, founder and CEO of Avicado. “Joining Accenture Construct lets us bring our specialist experience to more clients and programs and gives our existing clients access to Accenture’s global capabilities, industry knowledge and technology. I’m excited for our team to grow their careers at Accenture Construct.”
Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Accenture Analysts Raise Price Targets Amid AI-Driven Growth Strategy
Price action for Accenture showed strength after two analysts raised price targets following the company's AI-focused growth strategy. TD Cowen’s Bryan C. Bergin lifted his target to $201 from $193, while Susquehanna’s James Friedman raised his to $230 from $210. The firm outlined a multi-year plan targeting revenue growth, margin expansion, and shareholder returns. Accenture expects mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027 and 2028, with acceleration in 2029. Free cash flow and operating margin expansion remain key goals. The stock now appears to be testing new support and resistance levels.
TD Cowen analyst Bryan C. Bergin raised Accenture's price target from $193 to $201 while keeping a Hold rating. Susquehanna analyst James Friedman raised Accenture's price target from $210 to $230 while maintaining a Neutral rating. The increases followed Accenture's Investor Day on Wednesday. Accenture outlined a multi-year strategy focused on revenue growth, continued margin expansion, strong free cash flow and shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases.
Accenture expects mid-single-digit revenue growth in local currency in fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028. Accenture expects growth to accelerate to mid- to high-single-digit growth in fiscal 2029. Accenture targets annual operating margin expansion of 10 to 30 basis points throughout fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029. Accenture expects a free cash flow-to-net income ratio of at least 1.1 times in fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028. Accenture expects that ratio to rise to 1.2 to 1.3 times in fiscal 2029. Accenture also targets at least $9.5 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2029.
Accenture plans to return cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Accenture targets a dividend payout ratio in the mid-40% range of prior-year net income in fiscal 2027. Accenture targets a dividend payout ratio in the high-40% range in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029. Accenture targets 5% dividend-per-share growth in fiscal 2027. Accenture targets $5.5 billion in share repurchases in fiscal 2027. Accenture expects repurchases to exceed share issuances in both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.
Bergin said Accenture presented a clear growth strategy as enterprise AI adoption expands. Bergin highlighted opportunities in capital projects, data and AI services, mid-market clients and operational technology cybersecurity. However, investors remain focused on whether Accenture can accelerate growth despite AI-driven efficiencies. Execution in fiscal 2027 will be crucial to validating Accenture's growth outlook. Accenture's multi-year growth framework draws on experience across more than 18,000 AI projects and an increase in Data and AI engagements worth more than $50 million. Bergin added that the fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029 outlook depends on improving macroeconomic conditions and sustained mid-single-digit growth in Accenture's core business. Accenture's core business accounts for 94% of revenue. Ongoing modernization in enterprise resource planning, cloud, cybersecurity and data is expected to provide further growth opportunities.
Friedman said past technology shifts, including offshoring, cloud and digital adoption, reduced costs and replaced some IT services but also stimulated business-services demand, supporting Accenture's growth. Friedman expects AI to follow a similar pattern, with revenue growth accelerating in fiscal 2029. Friedman projects first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 2.5% to $19.2 billion. Friedman projects full-year fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 4% to $77.2 billion. Friedman forecasts earnings per share of $3.97 for the first quarter. Friedman forecasts earnings per share of $14.62 for the full year.
Revenue is expected to increase 5.7% to $81.6 billion in fiscal 2028. Revenue is expected to increase 7% to $87.3 billion in fiscal 2029. Earnings per share are expected to reach $16.00 in fiscal 2028. Earnings per share are expected to reach $17.78 in fiscal 2029. Operating margins are projected to expand from 16% in fiscal 2027 to 16.2% in fiscal 2028 and 16.4% in fiscal 2029.
Accenture shares were down 0.05% at $224.90 at publication on Friday.

Accenture, Dragos and SANS Institute Launch Foundation to Strengthen Cyber Defenses for Under-Resourced U.S. Utilities
Accenture, Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities.
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 12:59 PM CDT 7 min read
Approximately $10 million in initial funding and services will support essential services relied on by more than 100 million Americans
Initiative will provide technology, deployment services and training at no cost to up to 500 under-resourced utilities
COLUMBUS, Ohio, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Accenture (NYSE: ACN), Dragos Inc. and the SANS Institute today announced a major initiative to help strengthen cyber defenses for under-resourced U.S. water, electric and natural gas utilities. These utilities provide essential services but often lack resources for adequate protection for their operational technology (OT) environments. The announcement comes amid a recent surge in cyberattacks targeting more than 100 U.S. water systems across over a dozen states.
In its first phase, the initiative will provide cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training free of charge to up to 500 under-resourced utilities. Accenture, Dragos and SANS are making an initial combined commitment of approximately $10 million in funding and services. In addition, Elastic is supporting the initiative through technology that allows for software delivery at scale by providing the primary log storage and query engine within the Dragos Platform.
Many of the tens of thousands of small utilities across the U.S., particularly those serving rural or underserved communities, face limited funding, workforce shortages and aging technology. This leaves the pumps, valves, substations and distribution networks that support essential services vulnerable to cyberattacks that can threaten public safety.
To address this gap, Accenture, Dragos and SANS are launching the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation to provide eligible utilities with OT cybersecurity technology, deployment support, hardware and training. The initiative builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which provides more than 100 utilities with free access to the Dragos Platform. The foundation was announced at a roundtable discussion focused on strengthening the cybersecurity of utilities in Ohio, hosted by American Electric Power (AEP) subsidiary Ohio Power Company, Accenture and Dragos.
"Our work with America's critical infrastructure operators has shown both the gravity of the cyber threats they face and a widening vulnerability gap—between large operators with the resources to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack those means," said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. "Together with Dragos and SANS, we will provide under-resourced utilities with the technology, expertise and training they need to better power and protect the communities they serve."
"Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats," said Robert M. Lee, Chairman, CEO, and Founder of Dragos. "The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost."
Eligible participants include U.S. based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue. More than 97% of utilities fall below this threshold, representing more than 50,000 organizations that may need support. Participants can expect:
Access to the Dragos Platform and services to help organizations know what's on their networks and how to address vulnerabilities and threats. Elasticsearch provides the underlying log storage and search capabilities that help Dragos deliver the platform at scale to participating utilities.
Accenture deployment services including expert configuration, integration and ongoing support.
SANS ICS/OT training to build and sustain in-house capabilities.
Hardware and infrastructure funding to purchase the equipment needed to deploy and run the Dragos Platform.
Peer community access connecting participants to a network of utilities sharing operational experience.
"The best security technology in the world won't protect a utility if its staff are not able to use it. The foundation puts training and skills in the hands of the people protecting the water, power, natural gas, and wastewater treatment systems that communities rely on," said James Lyne, CEO, SANS.
"Strong cybersecurity depends on many technologies working together. Elastic is committed to supporting Dragos in delivering its platform at scale, helping make advanced cybersecurity capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them," said Ashutosh Kulkarni, CEO, Elastic.
Utilities interested in participating can learn more at https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
About the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation
The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation is a nonprofit launched by Accenture, Dragos, and the SANS Institute. It raises and provides the funding, hardware, deployment services, and training that small, under-resourced utilities in the U.S. need to secure their operational technology environments. Visit https://www.ccrfoundation.org/.
